questions.prompt: What can 200 MΩ also be expressed as?
questions.explanation: The SI prefix mega (M) denotes 10⁶, so 200 MΩ equals 200 × 10⁶ Ω.

A.text: The nano prefix is 10⁻⁹, so this expression represents only 200 nΩ rather than 200 megaohms.

B.text: A factor of 10⁹ is the giga scale, making this value one thousand times larger than 200 MΩ.

C.text: The factor 10⁻⁶ denotes the micro scale; it reverses the required positive exponent for mega.

D.text: The SI prefix mega (M) denotes 10⁶, so 200 MΩ equals 200 × 10⁶ Ω.

questions.prompt: A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of 10 cm and one shorter side of 8 cm. What is the length of the other side, a?
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras, a = √(10² − 8²) = √36 = 6 cm.

A.text: A 12 cm leg would be longer than the stated 10 cm hypotenuse, which is impossible in a right-angled triangle.

B.text: Subtracting 8 directly from 10 gives 2, but Pythagoras requires the difference of the squared lengths.

C.text: By Pythagoras, a = √(10² − 8²) = √36 = 6 cm.

D.text: A 9 cm leg would give 8² + 9² = 145, not the hypotenuse square of 10² = 100.

questions.explanation: Volume is length x width x height. 3 m x 8 m x 2.4 m = 57.6 m³.

A.text: This value is neither the product 3 × 8 × 2.4 nor expressed in the cubic units required for volume.

B.text: Cubic metres are the right dimension, but 13.4 is not the product of the room's three stated dimensions.

C.text: The numerical product is correct, but square metres measure area; a three-dimensional room volume needs m³.

D.text: Volume is length x width x height. 3 m x 8 m x 2.4 m = 57.6 m³.

questions.prompt: Hertz is the SI unit of measurement for what quantity?
questions.explanation: Frequency measures how many complete cycles of an alternating quantity occur each second. The hertz is defined as one cycle per second, making it the SI unit for frequency; UK mains, for example, runs at 50 Hz.

A.text: Capacitance is measured in farads, whereas hertz counts the number of periodic cycles occurring each second.

B.text: Frequency measures how many complete cycles of an alternating quantity occur each second. The hertz is defined as one cycle per second, making it the SI unit for frequency; UK mains, for example, runs at 50 Hz.

C.text: Reactance is opposition to alternating current and is measured in ohms, not cycles per second.

D.text: Electrical resistivity is measured in ohm metres; hertz instead quantifies repetition rate or frequency.

questions.prompt: For a series AC circuit with resistance R and net reactance X, which formula gives the impedance magnitude Z?
questions.explanation: Resistance and net reactance are perpendicular components of the impedance triangle, so Z = √(R² + X²).

A.text: Subtracting the squared components cannot give the hypotenuse of the resistance-reactance impedance triangle.

B.text: R divided by X is a dimensionless ratio, so it cannot produce an impedance whose unit must be ohms.

C.text: Resistance and net reactance are perpendicular components of the impedance triangle, so Z = √(R² + X²).

D.text: X divided by R is also dimensionless and describes a ratio rather than the magnitude of vector impedance.

questions.explanation: A voltmeter must be placed in parallel so it measures the potential difference across the load. Its high resistance prevents it from significantly changing the circuit current.

D.text: An inverter creates an AC output from DC and is unrelated to connecting a voltmeter across the two load terminals.

questions.explanation: Weight is the gravitational force on a mass, so W = m × g.

questions.explanation: A claw hammer pulling a nail pivots about its head and multiplies effort at the handle. That is the action of a lever.

B.text: A claw hammer pulling a nail pivots about its head and multiplies effort at the handle. That is the action of a lever.

C.text: A pulley redirects a tensioned rope or belt around a wheel, neither of which is present when the claw pulls the nail.

D.text: A winch winds rope or cable onto a drum, while a claw hammer multiplies handle effort by lever action.

questions.explanation: Potential energy is stored energy due to position or condition. Kinetic energy is energy of motion, so it is not the stored form asked for here.

B.text: Kinetic energy is associated with motion; a stationary raised or deformed system can still store potential energy.

questions.explanation: Efficiency = output / input, so input = output / efficiency. 2.1 kW / 0.85 = 2.47 kW.

A.text: This is one quarter of the output and is even below 2.1 kW, whereas a machine below 100% efficiency needs more input than output.

B.text: Efficiency = output / input, so input = output / efficiency. 2.1 kW / 0.85 = 2.47 kW.

C.text: An input of 2.95 kW would give only about 71% efficiency, not the stated 85% relationship.

D.text: An input of 3.27 kW would imply roughly 64% efficiency and includes far more loss than the data specifies.

questions.explanation: Power to lift a mass is work done divided by time: mgh / t. 500 x 9.81 x 50 / 90 is about 2.7 kW.

A.text: This is ten times too small because it effectively loses a factor from the approximate gravitational acceleration.

B.text: Power to lift a mass is work done divided by time: mgh / t. 500 x 9.81 x 50 / 90 is about 2.7 kW.

C.text: A 37.5 kW result is not obtained from mgh divided by 90 seconds and overstates the lifting rate substantially.

D.text: A 55.5 kW result is about twenty times the required power and does not account correctly for the 90-second duration.

questions.prompt: What is the input of an electric motor with an output of 5 kW that has an efficiency of 80%?
questions.explanation: Input power is output power divided by efficiency. 5 kW / 0.80 = 6.25 kW.

A.text: Multiplying 5 kW by 0.8 gives the notional output from a 5 kW input, rather than the input needed for a 5 kW output.

B.text: This value is below the stated output, which would require an impossible efficiency greater than 100%.

C.text: An input of 6 kW would imply 83.3% efficiency, not the stated 80% efficiency.

D.text: Input power is output power divided by efficiency. 5 kW / 0.80 = 6.25 kW.

questions.prompt: Which atomic part flows when current flows?
questions.explanation: Electric current in metallic conductors is the movement of electrons. Protons and neutrons remain bound in the atomic nucleus.

D.text: Protons carry positive charge but are bound inside nuclei in a metal; the mobile charge carriers are conduction electrons.

questions.explanation: Copper has lower bulk electrical resistivity than gold, brass or lead. Gold is valuable for corrosion-resistant contacts, but it is not the best bulk conductor in this list.

B.text: Copper has lower bulk electrical resistivity than gold, brass or lead. Gold is valuable for corrosion-resistant contacts, but it is not the best bulk conductor in this list.

C.text: Gold resists surface corrosion and is excellent for contacts, but its bulk resistivity is higher than copper's.

D.text: Lead has much higher electrical resistivity than copper and is selected for other properties, not maximum conductivity.

questions.prompt: A conductor measuring 50 m in length has a resistance of 0.4 Ω. What would be its resistance if its length is reduced to 25 m?
questions.explanation: For the same material and cross-sectional area, resistance is directly proportional to length. Halving the length from 50 m to 25 m halves the resistance to 0.2 Ω.

B.text: Keeping 0.4 Ω assumes resistance is independent of length, contrary to R = ρL/A for unchanged material and area.

D.text: Doubling the resistance to 0.8 Ω would correspond to doubling conductor length, not halving it from 50 m to 25 m.

questions.explanation: Using R = ρL/A rearranged gives L = RA/ρ. 0.089 x 4 / 0.0178 = 20 m.

C.text: A 40 m conductor of the same section would have twice the stated resistance, approximately 0.178 Ω.

D.text: Satisfactory merely restates the premise without identifying the recognised requirement that equipment be suitable for its intended purpose.

questions.prompt: The procedure put in place by an employer to identify hazards in the workplace is called a:
questions.explanation: A risk assessment procedure is the employer's formal method for identifying hazards and evaluating risks. It leads to control measures before or during the work.

A.text: Hazard control survey is not the recognised management process that identifies hazards, evaluates risk and determines precautions.

B.text: A risk assessment procedure is the employer's formal method for identifying hazards and evaluating risks. It leads to control measures before or during the work.

C.text: Risk control follows assessment by implementing precautions; it is not the name of the preceding hazard-identification and evaluation procedure.

D.text: Safety assessment is a generic phrase, while UK health-and-safety guidance specifically calls the structured process risk assessment.

questions.prompt: In a capacitor start motor the capacitor is connected:

options.B: In parallel with the run winding
options.C: In series with the run winding
options.D: In series with the start winding

questions.explanation: In a capacitor-start motor, the capacitor is placed in series with the start winding. This creates a phase shift that produces starting torque.

A.text: A capacitor simply placed across the supply would not be in the start-winding current path needed to create the starting phase displacement.

B.text: Parallel connection with the run winding places it across the supply and does not form the required series auxiliary-winding branch.

C.text: Putting the capacitor in series with the run winding would disrupt the winding that must remain energised throughout normal operation.

D.text: In a capacitor-start motor, the capacitor is placed in series with the start winding. This creates a phase shift that produces starting torque.

questions.prompt: Which legal framework principally governs the handling of personal and special-category data in the UK?

options.A: Data Protection Act 2018 and UK GDPR
options.B: Health and Safety at Work Act

questions.explanation: UK data protection is governed principally by the UK GDPR together with the Data Protection Act 2018.

A.text: UK data protection is governed principally by the UK GDPR together with the Data Protection Act 2018.

B.text: The Health and Safety at Work etc. Act addresses workplace health and safety duties, not the detailed processing rights for personal data.

C.text: The Human Rights Act protects Convention rights but is not the principal operational framework governing controllers, processors and data-subject rights.

D.text: The Official Secrets Acts concern unauthorised disclosure of protected state information, not general personal and special-category data processing.

questions.prompt: When should a suitable and sufficient risk assessment be completed for work that may expose people to risk?

options.B: Only after machinery has been energised
options.C: Before work starts and reviewed when circumstances materially change

questions.explanation: Risks must be assessed before the work starts so controls can be implemented, and the assessment must be reviewed when it may no longer be valid or circumstances significantly change.

A.text: Waiting until after an accident makes the assessment reactive and fails to identify controls needed before anyone is exposed.

B.text: Assessing only after energisation is too late because machinery hazards and the necessary precautions must be considered before work begins.

C.text: Risks must be assessed before the work starts so controls can be implemented, and the assessment must be reviewed when it may no longer be valid or circumstances significantly change.

D.text: The employer's assessment duty applies without an HSE request; enforcement action is not the trigger for managing foreseeable risk.

questions.prompt: Which planning action specifically prevents different trades' scheduled activities from conflicting on a construction site?

options.A: Co-ordinate the activities of workers from all trades

questions.explanation: Co-ordinating the activities of all trades prevents overlapping work from creating access, sequencing or safety conflicts. Competence is also required, but it is a separate management duty rather than the scheduling action asked for.

A.text: Co-ordinating the activities of all trades prevents overlapping work from creating access, sequencing or safety conflicts. Competence is also required, but it is a separate management duty rather than the scheduling action asked for.

B.text: Worker competence is an important separate duty, but checking competence does not by itself coordinate the timing and interaction of different trades.

C.text: Equipment cost affects commercial planning but does not specifically prevent one trade's scheduled activity from creating conflict with another's.

D.text: Break arrangements may appear in a programme, but they are not the core coordination control for interacting construction activities.

questions.prompt: Which device commonly provides additional protection against electric shock under BS 7671?
questions.explanation: An RCD can provide additional protection by disconnecting when residual current reaches its operating threshold. The current BS 7671 term is additional protection, not supplementary protection.

A.text: A BS 88 fuse responds to overcurrent and cannot detect the small line-neutral imbalance used for additional shock protection.

B.text: Cartridge describes a fuse construction; it still operates from excessive current rather than a residual-current imbalance.

C.text: A general overcurrent protective device protects conductors against overload and fault current but is not necessarily sensitive enough for additional protection.

D.text: An RCD can provide additional protection by disconnecting when residual current reaches its operating threshold. The current BS 7671 term is additional protection, not supplementary protection.

questions.prompt: What is the reactance of a 1 µF capacitor connected to a 50 Hz supply?

B.text: A milliohm result is one million times smaller than the calculated 3180 Ω and comes from mishandling the microfarad conversion.

C.text: This is ten times too large; substituting 50 Hz and 1 µF gives about 3.18 kΩ rather than 31.8 kΩ.

D.text: This is ten times too small and would correspond to a 10 µF capacitor at 50 Hz, not the stated 1 µF.

questions.prompt: When connected directly to a fixed-frequency supply, cage-rotor induction motors are generally considered to be:
questions.explanation: A directly supplied cage induction motor runs close to synchronous speed, with only a small load-dependent change in slip, so it is classed as substantially constant speed. Variable speed requires frequency control or another speed-control arrangement.

A.text: A directly supplied cage induction motor runs close to synchronous speed, with only a small load-dependent change in slip, so it is classed as substantially constant speed. Variable speed requires frequency control or another speed-control arrangement.

B.text: Operating speed is set mainly by supply frequency and pole count, so a cage motor is not inherently a low-speed machine.

C.text: Cage induction motors are produced across a wide torque range; low torque is not their defining speed characteristic.

D.text: A cage motor can be varied by a suitable drive, but direct connection to fixed frequency gives substantially constant operating speed.

questions.prompt: The main function of a fuse is to protect:
questions.explanation: A fuse is primarily there to protect circuit conductors from overheating under overcurrent or fault conditions. It is not the main device for electric shock protection.

A.text: A fuse may clear a sufficiently large earth fault, but it is not the general device for additional protection against electric shock.

B.text: Voltage spikes are transient overvoltages handled by surge-protective measures; a fuse responds to excessive current.

C.text: A fuse is primarily there to protect circuit conductors from overheating under overcurrent or fault conditions. It is not the main device for electric shock protection.

D.text: The consumer unit enclosure is not the load being protected by each final-circuit fuse; conductor thermal limits determine the fuse selection.

questions.prompt: The rotor conductors of a three phase cage rotor induction motor take the form of solid conductors:

options.A: Connected to the supply via conductors
options.B: Connected to the supply via slip rings
options.C: In series with the rotor windings
options.D: Shorted at each end by rings

questions.explanation: A cage rotor is made from solid bars shorted together by end rings. This forms the squirrel-cage circuit in which rotor currents are induced.

A.text: Cage bars receive no wired external supply; rotor current is induced by the rotating stator field.

B.text: Slip rings provide external access to a wound rotor, whereas a squirrel-cage rotor has permanently shorted end rings.

C.text: The bars themselves form the rotor circuit and are not separate conductors placed in series with another rotor winding.

D.text: A cage rotor is made from solid bars shorted together by end rings. This forms the squirrel-cage circuit in which rotor currents are induced.

questions.prompt: If the plates of a parallel plate capacitor are increased in area, the capacitance will:
questions.explanation: Capacitance is proportional to plate area. Increasing the overlapping area lets the capacitor store more charge for the same voltage.

A.text: For fixed separation and dielectric, C = εA/d shows that capacitance is directly, not inversely, proportional to plate area.

B.text: Capacitance is proportional to plate area. Increasing the overlapping area lets the capacitor store more charge for the same voltage.

C.text: Keeping capacitance unchanged ignores the additional charge-storage surface created when the overlapping plate area increases.

D.text: Increasing finite plate area cannot make capacitance vanish; zero would require removing the effective overlap or changing the circuit entirely.

questions.prompt: A transistor connected in common-emitter mode and biased into saturation will act as:
questions.explanation: In saturation the collector-emitter voltage is low and the transistor conducts strongly, so in the ideal switching model it behaves as a closed switch.

A.text: In saturation the collector-emitter voltage is low and the transistor conducts strongly, so in the ideal switching model it behaves as a closed switch.

B.text: A controlled rectifier is normally a thyristor-type function; transistor saturation here describes the conducting state of a switch.

C.text: Linear current amplification uses the active region, while deep saturation sacrifices proportional gain to obtain a low on-state voltage.

D.text: An open switch corresponds to cutoff with negligible collector current, the opposite of the heavily conducting saturation state.

questions.prompt: If an ideal pure inductor with reactance 100 Ω is connected across a single-phase 230 V AC supply, what average real power does it dissipate?
questions.explanation: For an ideal inductor, current lags voltage by 90°, so power factor is zero and average real power is 0 W.

A.text: For an ideal inductor, current lags voltage by 90°, so power factor is zero and average real power is 0 W.

B.text: This value is not obtained from P = VI cos φ; the ideal inductor has cos 90° = 0 regardless of its 2.3 A current.

C.text: Twenty-three kilowatts is incompatible with a 230 V source and 100 Ω reactance, whose current is only 2.3 A.

D.text: The product 230 V × 2.3 A is about 529 VA of reactive apparent power, not watts of average real dissipation.

questions.prompt: Earth leakage currents can occur naturally in electrical equipment, for example, cookers, fridges and freezers. This can cause nuisance tripping if the supply is controlled by a:
questions.explanation: Natural earth leakage creates an imbalance between line and neutral currents. An RCD senses that imbalance and may trip even when there is no hard fault.

A.text: A BS 1361 fuse responds to overcurrent and cannot compare outgoing line current with returning neutral current.

B.text: A cartridge fuse also operates thermally under excessive current, so normal aggregate leakage may remain far below its rating.

C.text: Natural earth leakage creates an imbalance between line and neutral currents. An RCD senses that imbalance and may trip even when there is no hard fault.

D.text: Solid-state device is too broad and does not identify protection that measures residual imbalance and trips the supply.

questions.prompt: Increasing the excitation, to the electromagnet in an a.c. generator will result in:
questions.explanation: Increasing excitation strengthens the generator field. A stronger magnetic field induces a higher output voltage.

A.text: Back emf is normally used for the opposing generated voltage in a motor; generator excitation directly raises the generated output emf.

B.text: Generator frequency is set by rotational speed and pole count, so increasing field current alone does not raise frequency.

C.text: Increasing excitation strengthens the generator field. A stronger magnetic field induces a higher output voltage.

D.text: Stronger field flux increases induced emf at unchanged speed, making a reduced output the opposite response.

questions.prompt: Which option lists the three broad loss categories in a DC machine?
questions.explanation: DC-machine losses are grouped broadly as copper losses, iron losses and mechanical losses such as friction and windage.

A.text: Copper and friction are genuine loss mechanisms, but capacitance and voltage are not broad DC-machine loss categories.

B.text: Current and voltage are operating quantities rather than loss categories, even though their product is used to calculate power.

C.text: DC-machine losses are grouped broadly as copper losses, iron losses and mechanical losses such as friction and windage.

D.text: Iron and copper are categories, but magnetic is vague and overlaps iron effects while omitting mechanical friction and windage.

questions.prompt: The centrifugal switch in a split phase motor is used to:

options.A: Disconnect the main supply to the start winding above full speed
options.B: Disconnect the run winding when approaching full speed
options.C: Disconnect the start winding when approaching full speed
options.D: Disconnect the starter at full speed

questions.explanation: The start winding is only needed while the motor accelerates. The centrifugal switch disconnects it as the motor approaches running speed to prevent overheating.

A.text: The centrifugal mechanism opens only the auxiliary start-winding branch as speed rises; it does not disconnect the motor's main supply.

B.text: The run winding must remain energised to produce torque after acceleration, so disconnecting it would stop normal operation.

C.text: The start winding is only needed while the motor accelerates. The centrifugal switch disconnects it as the motor approaches running speed to prevent overheating.

D.text: Starter is imprecise and waiting until exact full speed is unnecessary; the switch opens the start winding as running speed is approached.

questions.prompt: An electric heater dissipates a power of 3.0 kW when connected to a 230 V a.c. supply. The resistance of the heater is:
questions.explanation: For a resistive heater, R = V² / P. 230² / 3000 = 17.6 Ω approximately.

A.text: The numerical value near 13 is the heater current in amperes, found from P/V, rather than its resistance in ohms.

B.text: This resistance would dissipate about 3.38 kW at 230 V, which exceeds the stated 3.0 kW rating.

C.text: For a resistive heater, R = V² / P. 230² / 3000 = 17.6 Ω approximately.

D.text: A 35.2 Ω resistance would dissipate only about 1.5 kW at 230 V, half the stated heater power.

questions.prompt: In an ideal half-wave rectifier with a 5 V RMS sinusoidal source and a resistive load, approximately what peak inverse voltage must the diode withstand?
questions.explanation: The reverse-voltage peak equals the source peak in this circuit: 5 × √2 ≈ 7.07 V.

A.text: Ten volts is twice the 5 V RMS magnitude, but peak inverse voltage here is the sinusoidal peak, not a simple doubling.

B.text: Halving the RMS voltage has no basis in the reverse half-cycle and greatly understates the diode's peak stress.

C.text: About 3.5 V is 5/√2, which converts in the wrong direction; RMS-to-peak requires multiplication by √2.

D.text: The reverse-voltage peak equals the source peak in this circuit: 5 × √2 ≈ 7.07 V.

questions.prompt: A series RL circuit has resistance R = 20 Ω and inductive reactance XL = 15 Ω. What is its impedance magnitude?

A.text: Using resistance alone ignores the perpendicular 15 Ω inductive-reactance component, so impedance must exceed 20 Ω.

B.text: This value is not the hypotenuse of the 20 Ω by 15 Ω impedance triangle and would be below the resistance component.

D.text: Five ohms resembles the arithmetic difference between R and XL, but orthogonal impedance components are combined by squares.

questions.prompt: Which legislation provides the principal legal duties for preventing electrical danger while carrying out fault diagnosis at work?
questions.explanation: The Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 impose the principal work-related duties to prevent electrical danger. Compliance with legislation is a duty framework rather than a work method.

A.text: COSHH controls exposure to hazardous substances and does not provide the principal legal duties for electrical danger during fault diagnosis.

B.text: ESQCR chiefly governs public electricity-supply safety, quality and continuity rather than the conduct of an electrician diagnosing workplace equipment.

C.text: The Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 impose the principal work-related duties to prevent electrical danger. Compliance with legislation is a duty framework rather than a work method.

D.text: WEEE regulates waste electrical and electronic equipment at end of life, not protection from shock while fault finding.

questions.prompt: Why would a method statement be used by an experienced operative before undertaking work on an installation to diagnose a fault?

options.A: Ensure Health and Safety requirements are considered
options.B: Ensure effective billing of the work procedure or process
options.C: To monitor customer satisfaction for trade reviews
options.D: To reduce the cost implications of the work to be undertaken

questions.explanation: A method statement sets out the safe sequence of work and the controls to be used. Even experienced operatives use it to make sure health and safety requirements are built into the task.

A.text: A method statement sets out the safe sequence of work and the controls to be used. Even experienced operatives use it to make sure health and safety requirements are built into the task.

B.text: Billing may use a record of work completed, but a method statement's safety purpose is to define the controlled sequence before the task.

C.text: Customer-review monitoring is a commercial feedback activity and cannot replace the task-specific precautions set out in a method statement.

D.text: A safe method may also improve efficiency, but reducing cost cannot displace the controls required to prevent injury.

questions.prompt: Which HSE guidance covers the selection and use of test probes and leads for low-voltage fault finding?
questions.explanation: GS38 is HSE guidance on electrical test equipment, including probe-tip exposure, lead construction, ratings and safe use; it is guidance, not a British Standard.

A.text: BS 3036 is a product standard associated with semi-enclosed fuses and provides no general specification for modern test probes and leads.

B.text: BS 7671 sets installation requirements, while the HSE document specifically addressing safe low-voltage test equipment is GS38.

C.text: IET Guidance Note 3 covers inspection and testing practice broadly; it is not the named HSE guidance focused on probe and lead construction.

D.text: GS38 is HSE guidance on electrical test equipment, including probe-tip exposure, lead construction, ratings and safe use; it is guidance, not a British Standard.

questions.prompt: Which document is appropriate when an existing circuit is altered to replace and relocate a faulty fan isolator, without installing a new circuit?

options.B: A Minor Electrical Installation Works Certificate

questions.explanation: A Minor Electrical Installation Works Certificate is intended for an addition or alteration that does not extend to providing a new circuit. A simple like-for-like repair alone does not automatically require that certificate, so the alteration is made explicit.

A.text: A condition-report inspection schedule records observations during an EICR; it is not the certificate for this completed alteration.

B.text: A Minor Electrical Installation Works Certificate is intended for an addition or alteration that does not extend to providing a new circuit. A simple like-for-like repair alone does not automatically require that certificate, so the alteration is made explicit.

C.text: A full EIC is used for a new installation, new circuit or work of that extent, while this alteration remains on an existing circuit.

D.text: An EICR assesses an existing installation for continued service and is not issued simply to certify one completed minor alteration.

questions.prompt: Who would an operative need to keep informed of serious faults found on the lighting circuits in a fully functioning commercial unit?
questions.explanation: Serious faults can affect the client's safe use of the building and business operation. The client or their representative must be kept informed so decisions can be made.

A.text: The test-instrument manufacturer needs reports about its equipment, not routine notice of installation defects affecting the client's premises.

B.text: A specialist manufacturer may advise on a particular product, but it does not control the commercial unit or authorise remedial work there.

C.text: HSE is an enforcement regulator and is not normally the first recipient of every serious defect discovered during contracted diagnostic work.

D.text: Serious faults can affect the client's safe use of the building and business operation. The client or their representative must be kept informed so decisions can be made.

questions.prompt: A client has reported that a number of space heaters have stopped working following extensive use during a cold spell. Which of the following items would be the most likely to be checked during testing for fault diagnosis purposes?

options.A: Circuit supply voltage and protective device status

questions.explanation: When several heaters stop after heavy use, first checks should confirm the circuit supply voltage and whether protective devices have operated. That quickly identifies loss of supply or overload tripping.

A.text: When several heaters stop after heavy use, first checks should confirm the circuit supply voltage and whether protective devices have operated. That quickly identifies loss of supply or overload tripping.

B.text: External loop impedance characterises the supply earth path at the origin and is not the first explanation for several heaters losing power after heavy use.

C.text: Phase sequence matters to rotating three-phase equipment, while insulation resistance is not the first check for a simultaneous heater outage.

D.text: Prospective short-circuit current is a protective-device duty characteristic and does not reveal whether the circuit presently has voltage or a tripped device.

questions.prompt: What is the most likely outcome following a small leakage between neutral and earth due to water ingress in the connections of a luminaire?

options.A: High earth fault currents causing the main DNO fuse to operate
options.B: High short circuit currents causing circuit fuses to operate
options.C: Phase sequencing becoming reversed causing machinery faults
options.D: Residual current flow to earth causing the operation of an RCD

questions.explanation: Water ingress can create a neutral-to-earth leakage path. The resulting residual current imbalance is likely to operate the RCD.

A.text: A small neutral-earth leakage is far below the large fault current needed to operate the distributor's main fuse.

B.text: The water path is described between neutral and earth, not as a low-impedance line-neutral short circuit that would operate a fuse.

C.text: Leakage at one luminaire cannot exchange the three line conductors and therefore cannot reverse phase sequence.

D.text: Water ingress can create a neutral-to-earth leakage path. The resulting residual current imbalance is likely to operate the RCD.

questions.prompt: What is the most likely reason for the sound of arcing within a contactor, controlling heaters, each time the load is on and running?

options.A: A dead short in the circuit

questions.explanation: Arcing heard only when the contactor is carrying load points to a loose or high-resistance connection. Load current makes the poor joint heat and arc.

A.text: A dead short would normally produce a high fault current and rapid protective-device operation, not continuing arcing only while the heaters run.

B.text: Arcing heard only when the contactor is carrying load points to a loose or high-resistance connection. Load current makes the poor joint heat and arc.

C.text: A genuinely low-resistance joint carries load without the local voltage drop and heating that sustain connection arcing.

D.text: A transient overvoltage is brief; repeated sound for the full period of load operation points instead to a current-dependent poor connection.

questions.prompt: Where is a short circuit in a cable most likely to be located?

options.A: An over tightened termination in an accessory
options.B: At the joint on the top of the circuit breaker
options.D: Where the containment has mechanical damage

questions.explanation: Mechanical damage is a common place for insulation to be crushed or cut. Damaged containment therefore points to the likely location of a cable short circuit.

A.text: An overtightened accessory termination can damage a conductor locally, but it is not as direct a location clue as visibly damaged containment.

B.text: A joint at a circuit-breaker may become loose or overheated, whereas the prompt asks where a cable short is most likely along the route.

C.text: A fall in ambient temperature does not normally cut or crush sound cable insulation and therefore provides no physical fault location.

D.text: Mechanical damage is a common place for insulation to be crushed or cut. Damaged containment therefore points to the likely location of a cable short circuit.

questions.prompt: What fault would an experienced operative suspect if the final socket-outlet on a radial circuit was not operating but the rest of the outlets on the circuit were?

options.A: Open circuit at the final socket-outlet on the circuit
options.B: Open circuit at the origin of the circuit
options.C: Short circuit at the final socket-outlet on the circuit
options.D: Short circuit at the origin of the circuit

questions.explanation: If all earlier outlets on a radial circuit work and only the final one is dead, the fault is likely at the final point or the cable feeding it. That is an open circuit at the final socket-outlet section.

A.text: If all earlier outlets on a radial circuit work and only the final one is dead, the fault is likely at the final point or the cable feeding it. That is an open circuit at the final socket-outlet section.

B.text: An open line at the origin would remove supply from every socket on the radial circuit, not only the final point.

C.text: A short circuit at the final outlet would normally operate the circuit protective device and interrupt the earlier outlets as well.

D.text: A short circuit at the origin would affect the complete circuit and operate protection rather than leave all preceding outlets working.

questions.prompt: What is the most likely reason for 15 A re-wireable fuse, protecting a radial socket outlet circuit that is reported to 'blow every so often'?
questions.explanation: A fuse that blows only occasionally usually points to intermittent overloading rather than a permanent short circuit. A short circuit would normally operate the fuse immediately each time.

A.text: A fuse that blows only occasionally usually points to intermittent overloading rather than a permanent short circuit. A short circuit would normally operate the fuse immediately each time.

B.text: An open line stops current and leaves outlets dead; it does not intermittently create excess current that melts a fuse element.

C.text: Metering accuracy at the intake affects energy recording, not the current-time operation of a 15 A circuit fuse.

D.text: A transient overvoltage is not the likely pattern after extensive heater use; accumulated load current explains intermittent overcurrent operation.

questions.prompt: Before diagnosing stairway lighting in an occupied multi-storey building with backup supplies, what should govern the safe system of work?

options.A: Ensure that all access equipment is non-metallic and tagged as 'safe'
options.B: Ensure that the emergency lights are functioning correctly
options.C: A suitable risk assessment covering occupied escape routes, emergency lighting and every source of supply
options.D: Ensure the standby generators are connected to the DNO supply

questions.explanation: The risk assessment must address the occupied escape route, continuity of emergency lighting and isolation of all normal and backup sources. Checking one feature alone is not a complete safe system of work.

A.text: Non-metallic access equipment may control one contact risk, but a tag alone does not address occupants, escape lighting or multiple supplies.

B.text: Confirming emergency lights is important, yet it omits safe isolation of backup sources and management of the occupied stairway.

C.text: The risk assessment must address the occupied escape route, continuity of emergency lighting and isolation of all normal and backup sources. Checking one feature alone is not a complete safe system of work.

D.text: A standby generator must not simply be connected to a DNO supply; changeover and isolation must prevent dangerous parallel operation or backfeed.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is the most likely test that will cause damage to sensitive equipment when testing to identify faults within an installation?

options.A: A continuity of protective conductors test
options.D: An earth fault loop impedance test

questions.explanation: Insulation resistance testing applies a relatively high DC test voltage. Sensitive electronic equipment can be damaged if it is left connected during that test.

A.text: A continuity tester uses a low test voltage and current, so it is much less likely to overstress connected electronics than an insulation test.

B.text: A PFC instrument performs a brief live loop measurement and does not apply the hundreds of volts DC used for insulation resistance.

C.text: Insulation resistance testing applies a relatively high DC test voltage. Sensitive electronic equipment can be damaged if it is left connected during that test.

D.text: A loop-impedance tester injects a controlled short-duration current; the distinctive damage risk here is the insulation tester's high DC voltage.

questions.prompt: What is the main risk when an operative undertakes live fault diagnosis work on an old piece of equipment containing electronic components?

options.C: That RCD testing may not be suitable
options.D: That continuity testing may cause damage

questions.explanation: Live fault diagnosis exposes the operative to live parts, especially in older equipment with less guarding or fragile components. Electric shock is therefore the main risk.

A.text: Live fault diagnosis exposes the operative to live parts, especially in older equipment with less guarding or fragile components. Electric shock is therefore the main risk.

B.text: Electronic equipment is not inherently a source of noxious fumes; the immediate hazard from exposed energised parts is current through the body.

C.text: Whether an RCD test is suitable is a test-planning issue, not the principal personal hazard created by live diagnostic access.

D.text: Continuity testing should be performed dead and may affect equipment if misapplied, but it is not the main risk during live diagnosis.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to have a logical sequence in respect of the stages of fault diagnosis and correction?

options.A: To avoid inconvenience to other contractors
options.B: To avoid wasting time and effort
options.D: To ensure compliance with the EaWR 1989

questions.explanation: A logical fault-finding sequence narrows the fault step by step. It avoids repeating tests, missing simple causes and wasting time on unlikely checks.

B.text: A logical fault-finding sequence narrows the fault step by step. It avoids repeating tests, missing simple causes and wasting time on unlikely checks.

C.text: BS 7671 supports safe verification, yet it does not make every efficient diagnostic sequence a specific compliance outcome.

D.text: EAWR requires danger to be prevented; the particular benefit of logical fault finding in this question is systematic use of time and evidence.

questions.prompt: Which voltage levels mark the upper boundary of the extra-low-voltage range discussed in GS38?
questions.explanation: GS38 states that systems below 50 V AC or 120 V DC reduce electric-shock risk to a low level. Above those boundaries, the full shock precautions for low-voltage test work are especially relevant.

A.text: This gives only the DC boundary and omits the separate 50 V AC level stated by GS38 for extra-low voltage.

D.text: GS38 is expressly guidance for low-voltage systems up to 1000 V AC; its probe precautions are not confined to high voltage.

questions.prompt: Which instrument is most appropriate for proving a three-phase AC motor supply dead after isolation?

options.B: A loop / PSC tester compliant to GS 38
options.D: A suitable two-pole voltage detector with GS38-compliant probes/leads, proved before and after use

D.text: A contact-type two-pole detector suitable for the system voltage is used to prove every supply conductor dead, and its operation is verified before and after the test.

questions.prompt: What is the correct unit that would be displayed on an RCD tester when confirming compliance with additional protection?
questions.explanation: The instrument displays RCD operating time in milliseconds (ms). Milliamperes describe residual-current magnitude, not elapsed trip time.

B.text: Milliamperes measure the residual test current, while the compliance result requested from the timer is elapsed time.

C.text: Megaohms are used for insulation resistance and do not describe how quickly an RCD disconnects.

D.text: The instrument displays RCD operating time in milliseconds (ms). Milliamperes describe residual-current magnitude, not elapsed trip time.

questions.prompt: What is the most appropriate method of finding the location of an open circuit in the cpc of a radial socket-outlet circuit supplying a number outlets?

options.A: Using a continuity tester at the mid-point of the circuit
options.B: Using a prospective earth fault test at the end of the circuit
options.C: Using an earth fault loop impedance tester at the origin
options.D: Using an insulation resistance tester on the supply to the circuit
